name: Stroq
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Windsurf, Antigravity and OpenClaw
short: Checks your coding agent's past sessions for commands that came from text it read and keys that left your machine.
what: Stroq reads your Claude Code and Codex sessions from the last 30 days. It prints a card showing how many commands came from text your agent read, which keys left your machine, and the moments worth a look, each with its evidence. It can also hook into your agent so every tool call is judged before it runs. The hooks deny `curl | sh` and outbound calls that carry a known secret, and they ask you first when a command repeats text the agent read.
who: Anyone who lets a coding agent run shell commands and wants to know what it actually did. The one-off card needs no install. The hooks are for people who want a filter in front of every action.

steps.title: See the card for your own sessions
steps.text: It reads your last 30 days of sessions, your key files and the folders your agent worked in. It prints key names, never values.

steps.title: Look at the evidence behind a moment
steps.text: Every moment on the card has its own `show` line.

steps.title: Check whether your keys went anywhere
Guard your next session
steps.text: This adds Stroq's hooks to your agent.

steps.title: Optional: open the console
steps.text: It is a private page on 127.0.0.1. Open the whole link it prints, because it carries a key that changes each time.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `npx @stroq/cli attack` to watch Stroq run 36 known attacks against your policy in a throwaway sandbox.

watch: Stroq reads your agent session transcripts and your key files. The README says it sends nothing, has no telemetry and writes only a small cache under `~/.stroq`.
`init` and the console change your agent's settings to add hooks. The console shows the exact file change first, and `npx @stroq/cli uninstall` removes Stroq.

Matching is text level, so a command the model writes from scratch does not trace back to a source. The README calls it a filter, and says a key can still leave in a script, a file or a variable without showing up.
Adding hooks from the console needs macOS or Linux. On Windows, use `stroq init`.
